input: Brainstorm a name for my new bakery

verdict.notes: Set B has two key weaknesses: Q5 ("short, easy to remember, and pronounce") violates atomicity by bundling three distinct asks, and Q6 (primary products) largely overlaps with Q1 (type of bakery), wasting a slot. It also misses high-value questions from Set A — notably whether the owner wants a personal/story-driven name and what location or community context the bakery will serve — which are essential creative inputs for brainstorming a name. The "(e.g., ...)" examples, while helpful, make some questions feel more like surveys than a natural coaching conversation.
